description: Curated SecHub Resources SC4S pack for VMware vSphere, ESXi, vCenter, VSAN, and NSX syslog routing. Extends upstream SC4S VMware vSphere inventory with conservative Library metadata, fixtures, Splunk knowledge, strict source-identification routing, and explicit validation gaps.

event_families.label: VMware NSX distributed firewall packet logs

normalized_fields.action: program, operation, fixture-derived family, or normalized NSX PASS/DROP/REJECT packet decision
normalized_fields.vmware_nsx_raw_action: raw NSX DFW PASS/DROP/REJECT packet decision token preserved separately from normalized action when present
normalized_fields.signature: result, NSX DFW rule token, eventID, or human message
normalized_fields.signature_id: eventID, NSX DFW rule token, or parser-specific identifier
normalized_fields.eventID: raw VMware RFC5424 structured-data eventID value preserved by Splunk KV parsing for structured-data fallback events when present
normalized_fields.op: raw ESXi/vCenter operation token such as Login or TaskEvent preserved by Splunk KV parsing when present
normalized_fields.user: raw ESXi/vCenter user value preserved by Splunk KV parsing when present before aliasing to src_user
normalized_fields.target: raw ESXi/vCenter task or login target value preserved by Splunk KV parsing when present before aliasing to dest
normalized_fields.severity: severity when present or safely derived from fixture-backed VMware service message text such as vmkernel or structured-data WARNING
normalized_fields.src: src parsed from NSX DFW src/port packet tuple when present
normalized_fields.src_ip: src_ip alias from NSX DFW src packet tuple when present
normalized_fields.dest: target when present in ESXi/vCenter task or login records; dst parsed from NSX DFW packet tuple when present
normalized_fields.dest_ip: dest_ip alias from NSX DFW dst packet tuple when present
normalized_fields.dst: raw NSX DFW destination-IP token extracted from fixture-backed packet tuples before aliasing to dest_ip and common dest
normalized_fields.src_port: sport parsed from NSX DFW packet tuple when present
normalized_fields.dest_port: dport parsed from NSX DFW packet tuple when present
normalized_fields.transport: proto parsed from NSX DFW packet tuple when present
normalized_fields.proto: raw NSX DFW protocol token extracted from fixture-backed packet tuples before aliasing to transport
normalized_fields.sport: raw NSX DFW source-port token extracted from fixture-backed packet tuples before aliasing to src_port
normalized_fields.dport: raw NSX DFW destination-port token extracted from fixture-backed packet tuples before aliasing to dest_port
normalized_fields.vmware_nsx_raw_direction: raw NSX DFW IN/OUT packet direction token preserved separately from normalized direction when present
normalized_fields.direction: explicit IN/OUT token from NSX DFW packet tuple normalized to lowercase when present
normalized_fields.src_user: user when present in ESXi/vCenter login events
normalized_fields.rule: NSX DFW rule token extracted from fixture-backed packet logs when present; surfaced separately from signature/signature_id for firewall-rule triage
normalized_fields.result: result when present in ESXi/vCenter task or login events

supported_transports.label: TLS syslog RFC5425
supported_transports.notes: Recommended SecHub Resources default for production import; use VMware ESXi/vCenter syslog forwarding or an intermediate relay for TLS where possible.

supported_transports.label: TCP syslog
supported_transports.notes: Use only where TLS is unavailable or terminated upstream.

supported_transports.label: UDP/BSD syslog
supported_transports.notes: Legacy/lab only. Upstream SC4S warns that load-balanced UDP can corrupt split VMware event handling.

source_log_version.name: VMware vSphere, ESXi, vCenter, and NSX syslog
source_log_version.notes: Grounded in upstream SC4S v3.43.0 parser/docs inventory and synthetic-equivalent fixtures. Real VMware version evidence is required before validation promotion.

validation.source_log_version: Upstream SC4S v3.43.0 VMware vSphere parser/docs inventory; synthetic-equivalent fixtures only
validation.evidence: Pack artifacts and fixtures are curated from upstream SC4S VMware vSphere source documentation, parser routing semantics, and public upstream/content-pack NSX DFW action-token evidence. No real ESXi/vCenter/NSX replay or Splunk read-back evidence is captured; quality_status remains curated and trust_level remains unverified.

required_splunk_capabilities: HEC token can write to required indexes
Search role can read required indexes

readback.spl: index IN (infraops, netfw) "SC4S_VMWARE_VSPHERE_TEST_" earliest=-2h | table _time index sourcetype source host vendor product action vmware_nsx_raw_action vmware_nsx_raw_direction direction signature signature_id severity src dest src_ip dest_ip dst src_port dest_port transport proto sport dport rule target user src_user result eventtype _raw

last_attempt.summary: Dedicated sc4s-validation-lab replay reached healthy Splunk TEST and SC4S TEST containers, created infraops/netfw indexes, and attempted to replay six VMware fixtures through TLS/RFC5425 127.0.0.1:20051. Splunk summary/detail read-back returned no matching fixture fields and the explicit count assertion observed 0 of 6 expected marker events. SC4S stats did not show VMware/vSphere/NSX fixture movement. This is a failed/blocked indexed-readback attempt, not validation evidence.

commands.splunk_summary_readback: index IN (infraops, netfw) "SC4S_VMWARE_VSPHERE_TEST_" earliest=-2h | stats count by index sourcetype source host
commands.splunk_detail_readback: index IN (infraops, netfw) "SC4S_VMWARE_VSPHERE_TEST_" earliest=-2h | table _time index sourcetype source host vendor product action vmware_nsx_raw_action vmware_nsx_raw_direction direction signature signature_id severity src dest src_ip dest_ip dst src_port dest_port transport proto sport dport rule target user src_user result eventtype _raw

splunk_requirements.knowledge_mount: packs/vmware_vsphere/splunk -> /opt/splunk/etc/apps/sechub_vmware_vsphere (writable in disposable TEST so Splunk bootstrap can chown app files)

explicit_gaps: live ESXi/vCenter/NSX source-version emission is not proven by this harness
malformed, split, or multiline VMware syslog behavior remains outside the fixture replay scope
VSAN-specific and broader NSX policy lifecycle events remain deferred until exact emitted-record evidence exists
collector wrapper, UDP/BSD forwarding, and production TLS forwarding behavior require separate source-shape validation

test_event_sets.label: VMware vSphere BSD/RFC5424 mixed syslog fixtures

timestamp_policy.primary_timezone: BSD fixtures require source/receiver timezone; RFC5424 fixture includes UTC offset
timestamp_policy.notes: VMware can emit malformed or split syslog; prefer RFC5424/RFC5425 or configure source timezone explicitly.

field_delimiting.field_separator: space-delimited key/value examples and RFC5424 structured data
field_delimiting.escape_policy: Synthetic-equivalent fixtures avoid secrets/customer identifiers and use RFC5737/example.test values.
field_delimiting.notes: Each line is self-contained; real VMware deployments may require grouping for malformed split events.

source.reference: Upstream SC4S generated entries vmware_vsphere, vmware_esx_json, vmware_esx_invalidmultiline, and VMware Lite addon entries; upstream SC4S docs/sources/vendor/VMWare/vsphere.md; upstream parser files under package/etc/conf.d/conflib/syslog, netsource, and post-filter; public upstream SC4S tests/test_vmware.py NSX DFW PASS packet examples; public VMware NSX Log Insight content-pack patterns for PASS/DROP/REJECT firewall decisions.
source.notes: Fixtures use RFC5737 and example.test identities and do not include customer samples, secrets, tokens, or proprietary Splunk TA content. NSX DFW fixtures preserve public PASS/DROP packet-token shape while keeping trust conservative until lab read-back exists.

curation.notes: Selected because demand research ranks VMware ESXi/vSphere/Aria as the highest current SecHub Resources coverage gap. Conservative pack only; validation evidence is still required.

src.notes: Present in NSX firewall examples when supplied; Splunk props surface the packet source as both src and src_ip.

dest.notes: Present as ESXi/vCenter task/login target or NSX firewall destination when supplied; NSX packet destinations are surfaced as dst, dest_ip, and common dest.

direction.notes: Explicit NSX DFW packet direction token such as IN/OUT, preserved as vmware_nsx_raw_direction and normalized to lowercase direction for fixture-backed packet logs only.

action.notes: PASS is normalized to allowed; DROP/REJECT are normalized to blocked for NSX DFW packet logs while the raw token remains available as vmware_nsx_raw_action. Other VMware families remain partial and family-specific.

signature.notes: Best effort based on public parser shapes, NSX DFW rule tokens, structured-data event IDs, and fixture-backed vmkernel storage warning text.

signature_id.notes: Structured-data fixture exposes eventID and NSX DFW fixtures expose the packet-log rule token; Splunk props surface these stable identifiers as signature_id where present. Real VMware/NSX read-back evidence is still required.

rule.notes: NSX DFW packet-log rule token extracted from fixture-backed packet logs and preserved separately for firewall-rule triage; not complete NSX policy validation.

severity.notes: Splunk props surface a derived severity field from explicit severity tokens such as WARNING in fixture-backed vmkernel and structured-data messages; not a complete VMware severity taxonomy.

user.notes: Present in synthetic ESXi/vCenter examples when supplied by the source; aliased to src_user for authentication-style searches.

result.notes: Present in ESXi/vCenter login or task examples when supplied by the source.

cim.notes: CIM mapping is intentionally partial for virtualization and network observability.

dst_endpoint.ip.notes: Mapped only when present in NSX firewall examples.

dst_endpoint.name.notes: Mapped when ESXi/vCenter examples expose a task or authentication target.

src_endpoint.port.notes: Mapped only for NSX firewall examples.

dst_endpoint.port.notes: Mapped only for NSX firewall examples.

network.protocol_name.notes: Mapped only for NSX firewall examples.

traffic_direction.notes: Mapped only when NSX DFW packet logs carry an explicit IN/OUT direction token; the raw token remains available as vmware_nsx_raw_direction and no direction is inferred for other VMware events.

activity_name.notes: Family-specific action/event label; NSX DFW keeps the raw PASS/DROP/REJECT token available separately from normalized action.

status.notes: Fixture-backed ESXi/vCenter examples expose simple result values such as success or completed; this is not a full OCSF status taxonomy.

metadata.uid.notes: Best-effort identifier mapping for VMware structured-data eventID and NSX DFW rule when present; not a complete OCSF event identity requirements.

rule.name.notes: Fixture-backed NSX DFW rule token only; no complete NSX policy inventory or rule lifecycle validation is published.

severity.notes: Mapped only when Splunk props surface a derived severity from fixture-backed service text carrying an explicit warning/error/notice token.

ocsf.notes: Optional OCSF mapping is not complete.

destination.ip.notes: Mapped only when present in NSX firewall examples.

destination.domain.notes: Best-effort destination/target name for ESXi/vCenter task or login examples; not a DNS guarantee.

network.direction.notes: Mapped only from explicit NSX DFW IN/OUT packet direction tokens; vmware_nsx_raw_direction preserves the vendor token while direction is normalized to lowercase.

event.action.notes: Best-effort action. NSX DFW raw PASS/DROP/REJECT is preserved as vmware_nsx_raw_action while normalized action carries allowed/blocked.

event.code.notes: Mapped only for structured-data fixtures that expose VMware eventID or NSX DFW fixtures that expose a rule identifier.

rule.id.notes: Fixture-backed NSX DFW rule token only; used for analyst grouping without stating complete NSX rule metadata.

log.level.notes: Mapped from the derived severity field only when fixture-backed service text carries explicit warning/error/notice tokens.

event.outcome.notes: Maps simple result values such as success when present; no full outcome taxonomy is published.

ecs.notes: Optional ECS mapping is not complete.

logging_presets.label: Basic VMware vSphere ingestion
logging_presets.description: Parser, dedicated listener env example, fixtures, and Splunk props. No drops, reductions, or multiline grouping.

logging_presets.label: Standard VMware vSphere knowledge
logging_presets.description: Adds eventtypes and tags for ESXi, vCenter, fixture-backed vCenter task completion, fixture-backed vmkernel storage warnings, fixture-backed structured-data fallback and warning discovery, fixture-backed login success, NSX, and NSX firewall searches with non-lossy NSX PASS/DROP/REJECT action-token normalization plus allowed/blocked analyst facets. No drops or reductions.
logging_presets.notes: Still non-lossy; enable after local review/import.

source_delivery.notes: ESXi/vCenter/NSX components natively forward syslog; relay may terminate TLS.
source_delivery.validation_status: metadata_classification_only; does not imply live replay/read-back validation

fluent_bit.notes: Fluent Bit support is recorded as a conservative collector/pipeline mapping only: native syslog listener or relay-to-syslog path; preserve the pack sourcetype/source routing and validate listener framing locally. No Fluent Bit config artifact is generated by this pack yet.
